t: You're at Willesden Jewish Cemetery, opened in 1873 and Grade II on Historic England's register. It has been called the Rolls-Royce of London's Jewish cemeteries, and also the Eighth of the Magnificent Seven. It has 29,800 graves, and four of its monuments are listed Grade II. One is the tomb of Rosalind Franklin, whose work was central to understanding the structure of DNA. Members of the Rothschild family are buried here too, among them the 1st Baron Rothschild and Walter, the 2nd Baron, who was presented with the Balfour Declaration. The Pre-Raphaelite painter Simeon Solomon is here, as are the film directors John Schlesinger and Michael Winner.
